figures.title: Chapter map: Q-fixed or V-fixed
figures.why: every capacitor question reduces to which side of the master fork you are on; the map hangs the 8 chapters off that first decision
figures.data: ch 1–2 charge & geometry → ch 3 energy & force → ch 4 combinations → ch 5 dielectrics → ch 6 RC transients → ch 7 advanced → ch 8 playbook
figures.read: chapters 1–3 are the base, 4–6 the JEE engine, 7–8 the Olympiad machinery and the strategy
figures.source: course overview (How these notes are organised)

figures.title: C = ε₀ × a length: geometry is the whole answer
figures.why: C depends only on geometry because there is nothing else for it to depend on — every formula here is ε₀ times one length
figures.data: plate ε₀A/d; isolated sphere 4πε₀R; shells 4πε₀r₁r₂/(r₂−r₁); coaxial 2πε₀L/ln(r₂/r₁); two-wire πε₀L/ln(d/a)
figures.read: scale every charge by λ and Q/V never moves — capacitance is just the linearity of Coulomb's law

figures.title: The master rule: which is fixed, Q or V?
figures.why: the answer changes the force, the energy change and the sign in one stroke; misassigning fixed-Q/fixed-V is the chapter's most expensive slip
figures.data: isolated: δW_mech = −d(Q²/2C); on a cell: δW_mech = +½V² dC (battery pays the other half); stable = lowers the appropriate potential
figures.read: a dielectric is sucked in, plates pull together, a movable plate snaps at pull-in — one rule, two branches

figures.title: Series = one shared island; parallel = one shared voltage
figures.why: the series rule is charge conservation at an isolated node, not 'same current'; parallel is equal voltage, not equal charge
figures.data: series 1/C = Σ1/Cᵢ with equal q; parallel C = ΣCᵢ with qᵢ = CᵢV; U_i/U = C_eq/C_i in series
figures.read: prove the rule from the island and you also learn exactly when it breaks

figures.title: Transients are three numbers
figures.why: V_C(t) = V∞ + (V₀ − V∞)e^(−t/τ) with τ = R_th C; two voltages and one resistance give you every RC answer
figures.data: open-capacitors → solve resistive net → close (V_C = node difference) → check island conservation; τ = R_th C (sources killed); V_C continuous
figures.read: V_C can never jump while the power stays finite — continuity is a consequence of finite power, not of capacitors

figures.title: Triage: configuration or conservation?
figures.why: ninety seconds deciding whether the question is about a configuration or about charge/energy conservation decides the whole method
figures.data: configuration asked → homogeneous medium: Gauss; inhomogeneous: matrix/map. Otherwise → single capacitor + resistors: three numbers; several plates: island charge conservation
figures.read: choosing force/energy when the geometry is trivial, or geometry when only conservation matters, is the commonest lost mark
